scene.goal: Get through the gate without an incident
scene.obstacle: Hannu's ledger and the palace audit
scene.turn: He gives directions and a warning instead of a fine

gate.text:
The gate is closing. The man behind the board has a stylus he has not yet wet and a piece of bread on the wall beside him that he has forgotten. He looks at your hands before he looks at your face.

"Name. Cargo. And whether you have been in this harbor before." He says it the way a man says a list he has said all day. Behind him a porter is arguing with a scribe about a jar, and neither of them is winning.

choices.text: Give your name, and the truth about your cargo.
Give your name, and say nothing about the cargo.
Show him the palace seal and say nothing.

ledger.text:
He writes. The **harbor tax** is three shekels for a man carrying oil, and nobody has ever explained why. You put them on the board and he counts them without looking up, twice, though there are only three.

"The **market** is up the hill. The inn is behind the **workshop quarter**. Do not sleep on the mole. The tide comes in and the harbor master will charge you for the rescue." He wets the stylus at last. "And keep your jars where I can count them. I am not asking twice."

choices.text: Ask where a person can find work.

silence.text:
"A man who will not give a name gives me a problem, not a crime." He writes something short, and the stylus scratches.

"Go on, then. The **market** is up the hill." He turns the board a little so you cannot read it. "And if you are still here at dark, do not be still here at the gate."

choices.text: Ask where a person can find work.

seal.text:
He looks at the seal for exactly as long as it takes to decide not to look at it. Then he looks at your face, and something in it closes.

"Then you are expected, or you are trouble. Either way, not at this gate." He steps aside, and does not wish you well.

work.text: "Work is the **harbor**, or the yard, or the loom. If you can write, the scribes at the gate will fight over you and then underpay you." He picks up the bread, looks at it, and puts it down again. "They always underpay you."

provenance.notes: The gate scene and Hannu are invented; harbor dues and gate scribes are period-plausible.
